summary: The plan is broadly well-shaped and internally consistent on the major load-bearing decisions (FOR-UPDATE-driven reservation, payment-callback dedup with terminal-state guard, Order as sole status writer, outbox-backed cross-service eventing). However the red-team surfaced four high-severity defects that must be repaired before fan-out: (1) reservation-expiry has no sweeper contract so abandoned checkouts leak stock forever, (2) the §11.2 shipping-fee tier (60 THB if subtotal<1500, else 0) is missing from BA scope and TL defaulted shippingFee to 0 — orders will compute the wrong grandTotal, (3) concurrent customer-cancel + payment-success crosses two Kafka topics with no global ordering, creating an Inventory commit/release race, and (4) cross-cutting.auth says the access token lives 'in-memory in the route handler' but Next.js route handlers are stateless per-request, so the actual token-acquisition path on each call is unspecified. Five medium findings around admin-cancel state semantics (BA wording vs §9.2), the soft-cancel stock-release assumption, frontend-web complexity tag, missing INV-004 abandoned-checkout AC, and order.update-status-admin's unspecified allowed fromStatuses also block. Plan-stage cap is 1 — BA and Tech-Lead must repair in one cycle or the run HardFails.

findings.locus: contracts.json#/contracts[name=inventory.reservation.create].payload_shape.expiresAt and absence of any expiry-sweeper or events.reservation.expired contract
findings.description: INV-004 requires that reservations expire and stock be released, and BA's in_scope keeps it. The contracts attach an expiresAt to reservation.create and define a RESERVATION_EXPIRED error code, but no contract owns the actual expiry sweep: nothing scans for reservations whose expiresAt has passed and triggers reservation.release. The only release paths today are payment.failed/expired/order.cancelled events. A customer who hits checkout.commit and then closes the browser without simulating leaves the reservation, and therefore the locked stock, in place indefinitely.
findings.recommendation: Add a sweeper contract — either a periodic system job (e.g. inventory.reservation.sweep-expired) that flips expired reservations to RELEASED and emits an events.reservation.expired event Order can consume to transition PENDING_PAYMENT→PAYMENT_EXPIRED, or assign that responsibility to payment via a payment-intent expiry timer that publishes payment.expired.

findings.locus: ba.json#/in_scope (checkout pricing entries) and ba.json#/non_functional vs requirement §11.2 'MVP Shipping Fee Rule'
findings.description: Requirement §11.2 specifies a tiered shipping fee — 60 THB when subtotal < 1500, 0 THB otherwise — as part of Pricing Rules, separate from §8.11 Shipping Mock (which BA correctly deferred). BA's checkout in_scope only states 'recomputes subtotal and total server-side' and does not capture the fee rule. Tech-Lead, with no BA signal, hardcoded shippingFee:'number (0 in MVP)' in checkout.preview. The resulting grandTotal will be wrong for any subtotal under 1500 — a directly observable functional regression against the requirement.
findings.recommendation: Add an in_scope entry and a dedicated AC for §11.2: subtotal<1500 ⇒ shippingFee=60, subtotal≥1500 ⇒ shippingFee=0, grandTotal=subtotal+shippingFee in this run (no coupon).

findings.description: Customer can race order.cancel-mine against payment-success: at t=0 the order is PENDING_PAYMENT; the customer hits cancel-mine while payment.callback fires concurrently. Order publishes order.cancelled (fromStatus=PENDING_PAYMENT) on ecom.order.events and Payment publishes payment.completed on ecom.payment.events. Both target the Inventory consumer with the same orderId partition key, but on different topics — Kafka does not preserve cross-topic ordering. If Inventory consumes payment.completed first the reservation becomes COMMITTED; then order.cancelled arrives with fromStatus=PENDING_PAYMENT and the documented handler 'release the (still-RESERVED) reservation' branch mismatches reality. Order itself is shielded by 'if not in PENDING_PAYMENT, ignore', but Inventory has no such state-aware guard against fromStatus drifting from current reservation state.
findings.recommendation: Either co-locate payment.* and order.cancelled on a single per-order-keyed topic, or make the Inventory consumer state-driven (look up current reservation state and act on the actual transition rather than trusting fromStatus). Document the chosen guard in events.order.cancelled.failure_modes.

findings.description: The contract says 'Frontend Next.js route handler injects this from HttpOnly refresh cookie + in-memory access token' and 'frontend never holds the JWT in JavaScript — refresh token is HttpOnly cookie, access token cached in memory by the route handler per request.' Next.js route handlers are stateless per request — there is no shared in-memory cache across requests. As written, the token-acquisition flow on every authenticated call is unspecified: does the handler call identity.refresh on every request, is the access token also persisted in an HttpOnly cookie, or is there a per-session edge cache? Each interpretation has different latency, security, and refresh-rotation implications, and Tech-Designers will diverge.
findings.recommendation: Pin the per-request token-acquisition path in cross-cutting.auth.transport — e.g., 'route handler reads HttpOnly access-cookie and HttpOnly refresh-cookie; calls identity.refresh only when access-cookie is absent or expired; rotates both cookies on refresh.'

findings.locus: ba.json#/in_scope entry 'order: Admin cancels an order before it ships (PENDING_PAYMENT or PAID)...' and acceptance_criteria[24]
findings.description: BA wording 'before it ships' is colloquial and a careful reader could include PACKING. Requirement §9.2 only lists PAID→CANCELLED 'only before packing' and does not list PACKING→CANCELLED, so PACKING→CANCELLED is forbidden by §9.3 by omission. Tech-Designer cannot tell from BA alone whether admin-cancel is permitted from PACKING, and Tech-Lead's order.update-status-admin contract reflects the same ambiguity (see PR-009).
findings.recommendation: Tighten the in_scope line and AC to enumerate: admin-cancel allowed from PENDING_PAYMENT and PAID only; admin-cancel from PACKING (or any later state) returns INVALID_ORDER_STATE.

findings.description: Requirement §9.2 row 8 (PAID→CANCELLED, Admin, reason required) is silent on the stock side-effect. Real businesses split on this — items may have been physically picked or even shipped from a 'PAID' state, so auto-restocking sold→available is a policy choice, not an obvious correctness rule. BA assumed auto-restock and Tech-Lead encoded it (events.order.cancelled.failure_modes for fromStatus=PAID, plus inventory.reservation.release notes). The assumption is defensible for an MVP but it is an assumption.
findings.recommendation: Either add a non_functional / business-rule note that explicitly states 'admin cancel of a PAID order auto-restocks (sold→available) in MVP' and ties it to the AC, or split the AC into two — soft-cancel-with-restock vs soft-cancel-without-restock — and pick one for this run.

findings.description: frontend-web depends on 36+ contracts (every customer- and admin-facing endpoint plus all five cross-cutting contracts), is the sole owner of the cookie↔Bearer translation defined in cross-cutting.auth, owns Idempotency-Key generation and reuse semantics on the client, and is the integration surface for the entire Customer journey. The complexity_rationale's bracket of 'Next.js App Router with route-handler proxies and 7 service surfaces' undersells this: a defect in the route-handler auth path or idempotency wiring blocks every functional Customer AC. By the same yardstick that tagged checkout 'complex' for orchestrating ~5 sync calls, frontend-web is at least equivalent.
findings.recommendation: Promote frontend-web to complexity:'complex' so Tech-Designer fan-out routes it to the higher tier.

findings.locus: ba.json#/edge_cases (no entry covers 'customer abandons checkout without simulating')
findings.description: INV-004 is in_scope as 'on expiry stock is released back to available' but BA has no edge case or AC covering the abandoned-checkout path: customer hits checkout.commit, the order is created in PENDING_PAYMENT with a reservation, and the customer never simulates. Without an AC asserting 'after the reservation expiry deadline the stock is back to available and the order moves to PAYMENT_EXPIRED', QA-L1 has nothing to write a test against, and PR-001 (the missing sweeper contract) has no observable acceptance signal even after Tech-Lead repairs it.
findings.recommendation: Add an edge case: 'Customer hits checkout.commit but never simulates payment' → expected: 'within reservation TTL the order moves to PAYMENT_EXPIRED, reservedQty is released back to availableQty, and a status-history row is written.'

findings.description: toStatus enum lists PACKING|SHIPPED|DELIVERED|CANCELLED but the contract does not enumerate which fromStatuses are legal for each toStatus. Specifically: is PACKING→CANCELLED allowed (admin-cancel after packing has started)? §9.2 of the requirement says no (PAID→CANCELLED only before packing). The contract's INVALID_ORDER_STATE catch-all is correct but does not surface the rule, leaving Tech-Designer free to interpret. This pairs with PR-005 (BA wording) to compound the ambiguity.
findings.recommendation: Add a transitions table to order.update-status-admin (or reference §9.2 explicitly): PAID→PACKING (admin); PACKING→SHIPPED (admin, trackingNumber required); SHIPPED→DELIVERED (admin); PENDING_PAYMENT→CANCELLED, PAID→CANCELLED (admin, reason required) — all others 409 INVALID_ORDER_STATE.

findings.description: Handler ordering for the three callback shapes (replay-on-(intentId, providerStatus), terminal-with-different-status, fresh-callback) is described in prose across idempotency_rules and notes but never as a single ordered checklist. Functionally specified, but Tech-Designer benefit from a 1-2-3 step list.
BA states the order number format ORD-YYYYMMDD-NNNNNN in_scope but no AC pins the regex/pattern. If any external system parses orderNumber this matters; for MVP it is advisory.

Tech-Lead added events.product.created beyond what BA requested, so Inventory can seed stock_levels(sku) for new products. Structurally necessary (otherwise inStock filtering breaks for new SKUs) and the assumption is defensible — capturing for traceability only.

Concurrent same-SKU adds from two devices should merge cleanly. The mechanism (unique constraint on (cart_id, product_id) + INSERT…ON CONFLICT UPDATE qty=qty+excluded.qty in one tx, or row-lock-and-update) is not specified. Tech-Designer can resolve, but a one-line note prevents divergent implementations.

findings.locus: contracts.json#/contracts[name=catalog.product.detail].failure_modes notes ('still resolvable for admin and historical-order paths')
findings.description: The 'historical-order paths' phrasing is misleading — order_items already persist productNameSnapshot, productImageUrlSnapshot, priceSnapshot per cross-cutting.persistence, so Order detail does not actually call catalog for DELETED products. The note can be tightened to 'admin-context only' to avoid misleading Tech-Designer toward an unnecessary Order→Catalog cross-call.
